name: Bremen
summary_text: Covered by the dedicated country dossier, which located no Bremen-specific trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding; the city-state operates on the national federal framework (federal criminal law, the general equality act, the 2024 self-determination law administered through its own registry offices), and no Land-level reform item was identified for it.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (anti-bot 'Access denied' interstitial); per the country dossier this 16 July 2026 France24/wire report covers the neo-Nazi prisoner (the 'Liebich' case) placed in a men's prison despite a legal gender change - the event that drove Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia to launch a Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act. Framework-level for every Land, since prison administration and registry offices are Land competences.

sources.title: Selbstbestimmung hinter Gittern
sources.claim_summary: Verfassungsblog constitutional-law essay (Clara Wellhäußer, 18 March 2026, 'Selbstbestimmung hinter Gittern') on how the Länder are rewriting prison-execution codes for trans inmates: a majority of the 16 states - the essay names Rhineland-Palatinate (new § 17 LJVollzG in force 1 March 2026), Bavaria, Saxony and Hamburg - have replaced placement rules unchanged since the 1970s, all anchoring placement to the civil-registry sex entry, which the author argues is constitutionally avoidable (self-declaration would suffice) and partly doubtful. A resident-detention analysis applying nationwide, not a visitor-facing per-Land deviation.

sources.title: How German prisons deal with trans inmates
sources.claim_summary: DW report (23 August 2023) on German prisons and trans inmates: climate activist Penelope Frank, a trans woman whose legal sex is male, faces placement in a men's prison; the prison-staff union's federal chair says men's prisons are inadequately prepared and understaffed (some 2,000 officer shortage; ~60,000 inmates in nearly 200 facilities); prisons are Länder jurisdiction and some states run special facilities or guidelines. National framework context for all 16 units.
